chunk_findings.detail: `_merge_file` treats *any* output on stderr as a fatal merge error: `code = -1 if r.err or r.code < 0 else r.code`. But `git merge-file` writes `warning: N conflicts during merge` to stderr by default whenever it leaves conflict markers (that is exactly what the `-q|--quiet` option, "do not warn about conflicts", suppresses; the code never passes `-q`). So for the mixed-block path, which is run *without* `--ours` and therefore is *supposed* to leave markers, every real prose conflict produces a non-empty `r.err`, `_merge_file` returns `-1`, and `merge_pin_text` hits `if code < 0: return ours, False` — discarding the entire merged byte string and handing back our file unchanged, with `conflicted=False`. Concretely: README.md is in `[pins]` and contains a `<!-- ddflow:begin TABLE ... -->` block; on our branch we edit prose line 1, on the other branch a *different* prose line is edited and line 2 is also edited (a genuine conflict). Expected result per the module docstring ("a real prose conflict stays a conflict") is a file containing conflict markers plus both sides' non-conflicting prose; the actual result is our README.md verbatim with `conflicted=False`, so `merge_into` reports a clean merge, the driver exits 0, and the other branch's non-conflicting prose edit is silently dropped — the exact B86a970f727 failure the change claims to fix. Note this also means `code > 0` is effectively unreachable here, so the intended "conflict" verdict is never produced. The same conflation makes the no-block branch fall back to `ours` on `--ours` conflicts (line 55) instead of using the merged text git produced.

chunk_findings.detail: The change describes the driver as running `git merge-file --ours %A %O %B`. `--ours` is the same "favor" mode that `git merge -Xours` uses: conflicting hunks are auto-resolved cleanly in favour of our side, i.e. the conflicting region of the *other* side is discarded and no `<<<<<<<`/`>>>>>>>` markers are written (and the merge is reported clean). Concretely: branch `one` edits `Middle one.` → `Mine.`, branch `two` edits `Middle one.` → `Theirs.`, both regenerate, then `merge(mixed, "two")` runs the driver on `doc.md` with `%A`=`Mine.`, `%O`=`Middle one.`, `%B`=`Theirs.`. The driver emits `Mine.` with no conflict markers, so the working-tree `doc.md` contains neither `<<<<<<<` nor `Theirs.`, and the merge succeeds — every assertion in this test (`done.returncode != 0`, `"<<<<<<<" in text`, `"Theirs." in text`) fails. Worse, the behavior the test is guarding against is exactly what happens: the other side's conflicting prose edit is silently overwritten with ours, which is the same silent-loss class as the bug being fixed (B86a970f727), just narrowed to conflicting hunks. Either the test's premise (conflicts remain conflicts) is wrong, or the described driver implementation cannot satisfy it; as written, the regression suite contains a test that cannot pass against the fix it accompanies.

chunk_findings.detail:
`code = -1 if r.err or r.code < 0 else r.code` classifies *any* stderr output as a fatal merge error. `git merge-file` does not take `-q|--quiet` here, and by default it writes `warning: N conflicts during merge` to stderr precisely when it leaves conflict markers — i.e. exactly in the case the new code path must handle. Concrete input: `README.md` is listed in `[pins]`, both sides edit the same prose line (`Middle one.` → `Mine.` / `Theirs.`), and the helper is invoked as `PT.merge_pin_text(ours, base, theirs)` from `_merge_pin_text`. `git merge-file` exits 1 with one non-empty stderr line; `r.err` is truthy, so `code` becomes `-1` and the genuine "conflict left in the output" result is collapsed into "driver crashed" instead of being surfaced as `conflicted=True`. `_merge_pin_text` then cannot distinguish the conflict-to-keep case the change is built around (it returns `False`/aborts on both branches, or, if `merge_pin_text` propagates the error, raises out of `_integrate` before the `merge --abort` fallback runs). This finding is not answered by the diff: part 1 only routes the merge-queue path through `PT.merge_pin_text` and adds neither `-q` nor any relaxation of the stderr test, and the triage leaves it untriaged.

(The companion finding that the driver uses blanket `git merge-file --ours %A %O %B` and therefore silently resolves conflicting prose is answered by the same hunk: `_merge_pin_text`'s docstring and its `conflicted` / `return False` branch define the shared merge as "prose of both sides merged, our side of the generated regions, False when prose both sides edited conflicts", which is consistent with `test_a_prose_conflict_stays_a_conflict` and inconsistent with a whole-file `--ours`; I am not reporting it again.)

chunk_findings.detail: The new driver routes every mixed file (README.md, listed in `[pins]`) through `merge_into`, and the whole point of that path is that the prose is merged *normally* (no `--ours`, no marker suppression) so that a prose conflict both sides made stays a conflict — the docstring in this very diff now promises exactly that. But `_merge_file` still classifies any output on stderr as a fatal error (`code = -1 if r.err or r.code < 0 else r.code`), and it never passes `-q`. `git merge-file` writes `warning: conflicts during merge` to stderr precisely when it leaves conflict markers, i.e. on every real prose conflict — the case the new code is supposed to surface as a conflict. Concretely: branch A and branch B both rewrite the same README.md paragraph and both regenerate; `merge_driver(["A","O","B"])` reaches `merge_into(...)` → `_merge_file`, git emits the conflict markers plus the warning on stderr, and the returned code is forced to `-1` (an error) instead of the positive "N conflicts" value, so `merge_into` / `merge_driver` no longer distinguish "prose conflict both sides edited" (expected: driver returns 1 and leaves markers) from "the merge tool blew up". The diff adds the mixed merge path but nowhere adds `-q`/stderr tolerance, so the regression this change is built around cannot be signalled correctly. (Previous finding 1, still holding: nothing in this revision answers it.)

chunk_findings.detail: A pin file that is not valid UTF-8 (e.g. a README.md containing a single stray Latin‑1/accented byte pasted by an author, or any byte sequence outside UTF‑8) is routed to the fallback, which returns `(ours, False)`: the driver writes *our* whole file and reports *no conflict*, so git stages it and the other side's prose edits are dropped silently — exactly the failure mode B86a970f727 is about (`services/pins_merge.py` returning 0 with ours untouched). Note this is not the "git cannot merge this content" case the docstring describes: `_merge_file`'s error path (checked with `code < 0`) already covers unmergeable content, and even if it did not, reporting `conflicted=False` is what makes the loss silent rather than a conflict the user has to resolve. Input that demonstrates it: base = mixed `README.md` (prose + `<!-- ddflow:begin T -->…<!-- ddflow:end T -->`), ours unchanged, theirs edits a prose line *and* a byte in the file is 0xE9 (Latin‑1 `é`): `merge_pin_text` returns ours, `merge_into` returns `False`, git treats the merge as resolved and theirs's prose edit is gone with no marker. At minimum this branch must signal a conflict (return `(ours, True)`) so the loss is not silent.

chunk_findings.detail: `_merge_file` still computes `code = -1 if r.err or r.code < 0 else r.code`, i.e. it treats *any* output on stderr as a fatal error. `git merge-file` (which is invoked here without `-q|--quiet`) writes `warning: N conflicts during merge` to stderr by default on every merge that leaves conflict markers, which is exactly what this mixed-block path is supposed to do. Concrete failure: two branches edit the same pins block, `_merge_file` merges them, `merge-file` exits with the positive conflict count and prints the warning, `r.err` is non-empty, and the function returns `-1` — the caller sees a fatal error instead of "merged with N conflicts", even though the marker file was written correctly. Nothing in the shown diff changes this expression or passes `-q`, so the earlier finding is not answered.

chunk_findings.detail: The change states the driver should run `git merge-file --ours %A %O %B`. `--ours` is the favor mode (the same semantics as `git merge -Xours`): conflicting hunks are resolved silently in favour of our side, no `<<<<<<<`/`>>>>>>>` markers are emitted and the merge is reported clean (exit 0). Concrete case: branch `one` changes `Middle one.` to `Mine.`, branch `two` changes it to `Theirs.`, then `merge(mixed, "two")` — the result contains `Mine.` with no markers, so a test asserting that the prose conflict "stays a conflict" fails against this implementation. It also fails against the *unfixed* driver (which leaves ours untouched, likewise without markers), so this test cannot be the required regression test that fails before and passes after; either the driver must not use `--ours` (leave markers and let the post-merge step regenerate the generated blocks) or the test's expectation is wrong. The earlier finding is unrefuted by anything in the shown diff.
